name: Drummond Company

summary.text: Drummond Company is a privately held coal producer based in Birmingham, Alabama. In 2018 a federal jury convicted its vice president of government and regulatory affairs, David Roberson, together with Balch & Bingham partner Joel Gilbert, of bribing state representative Oliver Robinson through a $360,000 consulting contract routed through Robinson's foundation, in exchange for opposing EPA Superfund action in north Birmingham. Robinson pleaded guilty; the Eleventh Circuit affirmed the convictions in 2020. The company itself was not charged.

facts.claim: A federal jury in 2018 convicted Drummond vice president David Roberson and Balch & Bingham partner Joel Gilbert of bribery, honest services wire fraud, conspiracy and money laundering for bribing state legislator Oliver Robinson.
facts.quote: A jury found former Balch & Bingham partner Joel Iverson Gilbert and former Drummond Company Vice President of Government and Regulatory Affairs David Lynn Roberson guilty of bribery, honest services wire fraud, conspiracy, and money laundering.

facts.claim: Prosecutors said the payments came from Balch & Bingham and Drummond, in the form of a consulting contract that paid Robinson $360,000 through the Oliver Robinson Foundation between 2015 and 2016.
facts.quote: The bribe came in the form of a consulting contract that paid Robinson $360,000 through the Oliver Robinson Foundation, a non-profit organization, between 2015 and 2016.

facts.quote: Those acts included advocating the Balch and Drummond position in a meeting with the EPA, using talking points drafted by Gilbert and secretly recording the meeting.

openQuestions: Site claim (convicted; Drummond VP and Balch partner convicted of bribing Oliver Robinson to oppose EPA Superfund cleanup in a mostly Black North Birmingham neighborhood; Robinson pleaded guilty; convictions upheld): supported, except the neighbourhood's demographics, which were not in the sources used.
DOJ releases give $360,000 and $375,000 in different places for the contract amount.
Drummond Company itself was not charged; this file records conduct of its executive and counsel.
